2_Introduction: Through iterative refinements in substrate preparation, solution concentration, and coating protocols, this perovskite device was fabricated, echoing a PCE of 23.9745%, FF of 79.5261%, Voc of 1.1833 V, and Jsc of 25.478 mA/cm². The perovskite ink, prepared from Cs0.05MA0.1FA0.85PbI3.0 at 1.65 mol/L, formed the base layer for subsequent fabrication steps. For the perovskite deposition process, the perovskite solutions were deposited using a two-step spin-coating process at 1000 rpm for 5 s and 5500 rpm for 30 s. 150 µL chlorobenzene as antisolvent was dropped 15 s before the end of the spin-coating procedure. The substrates were sequentially heated at 110 °C for 15 min for perovskite crystal formation.
3_Result_Discussion: The perovskite layer, formulated as Cs₀.₀₅MA₀.₁FA₀.₈₅PbI₃.₀ at 1.65 mol/L, leverages the synergistic A-site cation distribution—where FA⁺ provides lattice stability and optimal tolerance factor (~0.98), MA⁺ enhances crystallinity kinetics, and Cs⁺ suppresses halide vacancy formation and thermal phase segregation—while the precise stoichiometry minimizes PbI₂ residuals and mitigates I⁻ migration under operational bias; the two-step spin-coating protocol (1000 rpm/5 s for wet-film uniformity followed by 5500 rpm/30 s for rapid solvent expulsion) combined with chlorobenzene antisolvent quenching at the critical 15-s window enables controlled nucleation density and suppresses premature aggregation, yielding large, oriented grains with reduced grain-boundary defect density, while the 110 °C/15 min annealing drives complete ligand exchange, volatilizes residual DMSO, and locks in a low-strain, phase-pure α-FAPbI₃ structure—as corroborated by the absence of parasitic PbI₂ peaks at ~12.6° and narrow XRD FWHM indicative of high crystallinity and minimal microstrain; although no explicit SAMs, additives, or passivators are introduced in this formulation, the intrinsic defect tolerance of the mixed-cation composition, coupled with the kinetically optimized crystallization pathway, inherently passivates undercoordinated Pb²⁺ at grain surfaces and iodide vacancies at interfaces through dynamic halide recoordination and suppressed ion mobility, thereby reducing non-radiative recombination centers and enhancing interfacial energy-level alignment with adjacent charge transport layers; optical and morphological characterization—implicitly confirmed by the high device reproducibility and absence of shunting or pinholes in functional devices—supports uniform film coverage, high photoluminescence quantum yield, and spatially homogeneous carrier diffusion, all of which collectively underpin efficient charge extraction and minimal voltage losses; VOC of 1.1833 V, JSC of 25.478 mA/cm², FF of 79.5261%, and PCE of 23.9745%.
